recipes.name: Best-Ever Texas Caviar
ingredients_raw: 2 (15 ounce) cans black beans, rinsed and drained
2 (15 ounce) cans pinto beans, rinsed and drained
2 (15 ounce) cans white corn, rinsed and drained
1 red bell pepper - cored, seeded and finely chopped
1 green bell pepper - cored, seeded and finely chopped
1 (4 ounce) can chopped green chiles, undrained
1 jalapeno chile pepper, seeded and finely chopped

steps.text: Combine black beans, pinto beans, white corn, bell peppers, red onion, green chiles, cilantro, and jalapeño in a large bowl.
Whisk vinegar, olive oil, sugar, and garlic powder together in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then remove from heat. Set aside to cool for at least 10 minutes.
Pour vinaigrette over bean mixture; toss to coat.

raw_recipe.headline: Best-Ever Texas Caviar
raw_recipe.description: This cowboy caviar recipe for Texas salad is made with beans, corn, bell peppers, and chiles in garlic vinaigrette for a delicious party appetizer.

review.reviewBody: This is really good and everyone loves it! The first time I made this I left out the cilantro because one of the guests hates it, but I just made it with the cilantro and it was even better. Only change I made was to use 1/4 cup lime juice and 1/4 cup rice vinegar instead of the 1/2 cup rice vinegar, mainly because I really like lime.

The basic ingredients in this recipe are a great starting point. I added avocado, chopped tomatoes, and 1/2 tsp. chili powder. I wasn't able to find black-eyed peas so I used small garabanzo beans instead. Furthermore, instead of heating the the dressing ingredients, I treated it as a salad dressing and mixed it in a glass jar. This recipe is always a hit.

This is a sooo good.. I make this quite a bit for parties. It's so tasty I make it the night before so all the flavors can blend together. I have shared this recipe with a lot of friends an family.. thanks

Loved this! Try using Trader Joe's frozen roasted corn in place of the canned corn. Took the advice from other posters and used 1/4c. rice vinegar and 1/4c. lime juice. Served with Fritos Scoops chips.

This recipe is always a fantastic hit. To make this a bit healthier I use a quarter of the olive oil and instead of sugar use seven packets of Splenda. I also triple the amount of garlic powder. Don't rinse the white corn! It imparts a great flavor; the original recipe never had you rinse the corn, White corn is the secret ingredient. This recipe is fantastic with scoops but you can also eat it as a salad

I've made this like 20 times because everyone loves it, even the picky eaters. I think this is the only vegetables some of my relatives eat all year. I go a little stronger on the vinegar and lighter on the oil, and add a little salt. It tastes a lot better if you make it 12 hours ahead of the party so the flavors can meld together in the fridge.

I gave this 3 stars because I changed up the recipe to my own tastes. I made the sauce but after tasting it, the sauce is just way too sweet! Who wants sweet and sour Mexican food? I prefer spicy, salty, lime flavor myself. I didn't use canned beans (used dried and precooked myself), used fresh corn, roasted my own green chili's on the grill, added fresh diced avocado, white onions, fresh garlic and cilantro. I used a drizzle of olive oil, lots of fresh lime juice and some juice from a can of jalapenos I had on hand. I completely skipped the sweet bell peppers, sweet red onion, sweet vinegar, and sugar. Made my way, it was fantastic! Served it over barley I had precooked and then sauteed with garlic, CA chili and cumin. It made the best taco's ever! Thanks for the recipe. As a relatively new vegetarian I've been struggling to find things I can make with flavors I love that don't include meat. This recipe sparked my creativity and although I didn't care for it as written, it was a starting point for something I will make again and again. Thanks!

I enjoyed making this. I added chick peas and dark kidney beans too. I know it calls for two cans sweet corn, but I swapped out one can of the sweet corn corn with green chiles and the other with Mexican Sweet Corn. I made sure to reserve some of the Mexican Street Corn broth to add to the dressing to give it a smoky flavor. ( even added a drop or two of liquid smoke mesquite flavor… it was awesome) Not so much jalapeño or chopped chiles since we aren’t into too much heat. Also added a bit of lime. Love the sweet bell peppers. They add a great crunch as well as flavor. This is a truly wonderful… AND PRETTY DARN HEALTHY salad. Lots of flavor, and lots of protein too.

This was delicious. Some ate as a salad on their plate and others as a dip on corn chips. I followed the recipe with two exceptions, 1) cut the sugar in half, and 2) used black-eyed peas instead of pinto beans (it was for a New Year’s event). I thought it was still too sweet so will reduce the sugar or even leave it out when making again. The light dressing was the star of this version of this popular dish, but will probably add lime zest or juice on my next try. Thanks for a great recipe!
Tweaked with 3 cloves crushed garlic and 1 tsp ground pepper. Also substituted Black eyed peas for pinto beans. Used Rice Wine vinegar, and olive oil for healthier fat choices. Delicious !

Really like this! In fact, I just finished making it and am writing this review on just the taste test (or small bowl I had to have!). It will be even better after the flavors meld. I did not have jalapenos, which would be a great addition, but it is fine without. I also added a little fresh lime juice. Otherwise, made exactly as written. I did halve it, as I did not need as much as the full recipe called for. Agree with the other reviewer that said this is better than the Italian dressing version. Will be making this again!
This is delicious! I made it as written except used frozen corn. I will definitely make it again.
I added some lime juice to the mixture and it adds just a perfect little zing to the recipe.
No black eyed peas?
We love it and make it often!! Thanks
Added less sugar and more garlic powder
Raw green bell pepper and raw red onion detract vs enhance this recipe. Recipe needs work. Dressing recipe also needs work, too vinegar-y.
great
Great. I do add Rotel. I spaced and just mixed the dressing w/o heating. Still delicious
I like to make it a little sweeter with 1 or 2 tbsps of more sugar.
